title: Monthly controls reduced deep-earthquake pair excess by 80% in ComCat for 2000-2025, and the residual depended on the grid
abstract: We tested a published deep-earthquake pair excess with monthly regional controls. The fixed global ComCat snapshot has 785 events with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth greater than 300 km in 2000-2025. There were 175 same-year pairs within 200 km chord distance and seven days. Annual twenty-degree regional time shuffles gave a mean of 130.20 pairs; monthly shuffles gave 166.13. Monthly controls reduced the descriptive excess by 80.2%. In 9,999 draws, the primary monthly upper-tail p-value was 0.0213. Ten-degree and shifted twenty-degree monthly grids gave p-values of 0.0675 and 0.0825. The primary residual was confined to the first day. Only 332 of 785 event times could move in the monthly groups. Thus finer controls reduce the excess, but they also change the question and test power. The small residual depends on the grid. This is a conditional location-time test on reused records, not independent confirmation or a test of physical cause. Sparse groups, catalog errors, mixed magnitude scales and exchangeability limit inference. The package gives code, source hashes, aggregate results, all null draws, a static figure and an independent numerical audit. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Monthly regional controls raise the expected seven-day pair count toward the observed 175. Ranges describe conditional null counts, not physical-effect uncertainty.

citations.reason: Published annual regional pair benchmark; same source records. This work adds monthly controls.
Published lag decomposition informed the first-day check. Data overlap.
